title: Grunewald classes and teachers
summary: He describes night classes and teachers including Davenport, Quentin Batiste, Clyde Kerr Sr. and dean Cary Levine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Can we get back to, maybe I have some more questions about Grunewald's. How was it structured? Did you go to class from a certain time?

Oh yeah, you had about four classes that you had to go to. You had theory in one place, you had singing in another place, you had humming in another place. Mm-hmm. You had various classes that you went to, you know. Mm-hmm. I'd say within three hour course at night, you know. Mm-hmm. Three to four hour, four classes at night. So. And I think I went three or four times a week. I forgot, man, it's been so long. You're talking about years back.
Okay, and could you tell me some more about who your teachers were at that time?

Well, I know Wilders, but I didn't have to go to Wilders, Davenport. He taught trumpet over there. He had a lady named Ms. Jenkins, she taught piano. Mm-hmm. And another lady named Ms. Chatters, she and I, we went to school together. I don't know what she was teaching, but I didn't have to go to her. We had Quentin Batiste, he was teaching theory. He was teaching Schellinger. We had Clyde Kerr, Sr. He was over there teaching band stuff. Spencer, Mr. Spencer, he was teaching bass.

And they also had Mr. Fink, a German fellow. He was teaching bass over there. Oh, they had quite a staff over there. And like I said, the dean was, I called his name earlier, I can't think of it right now. He used to catch me coming down from the last class at night. Come on, Cotton, come on in here. And I'd sit down and I'd boom-ching, boom-ching for him while he played his clarinet. Cary Levine.

Cary Levine, he was a school teacher in the daytime, but he was also the dean of the school over here. So they had quite a staff over there, man. That's all I can remember. That's all I can recall because I only went to, let's see. I'd have to look in those books and find out exactly the class that I went to, you know. But I can remember going at least three or four nights a week at the school, you know.
Could you go and do it in the day? Was it only in the day school? That was the day school as well.
Yeah, it was the day school, but I worked in the day.
